title: Introduce adapter-based load benchmarking and CI matrix for perf regression
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: The current monolithic load runner (loadbench) mixes scenario orchestration, model adapters, and CI glue logic in a single codebase. This makes adding new model endpoints (quantized vs fp32), new transport protocols (grpc/http/stream), and CI matrix entries slow and error-prone. We frequently see flaky CI jobs when run in parallel and maintainers spend time patching bespoke adapters inside the runner.

Goal: Refactor loadbench into a thin orchestration core and a set of stable adapters (grpc, http, kv-cache aware, tokenized-input) with a documented plugin contract. Integrate the new adapter model into CI so perf regressions run across a constrained matrix (model family x sequence length x quant profile) and failures produce actionable artifacts (perf traces, flamegraphs, artifacts). Reduce CI flakiness and per-run maintenance burden.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter interface (python) defined and documented in the repo README and Confluence
Three adapters implemented and validated: grpc-sync, http-async, kv-aware-cacher
CI matrix defined and jobs run under a single pipeline with stable Docker images
Perf regression job emits token-latency distributions, 95th/99th percentiles and pulls artifacts into the test run
Demo migration of two legacy scenarios to adapter model with <5% variance vs baseline
Unblocked downstream eval pipelines (ENG-20345) and no increase in CI wall time >15% per run
plan: 1) Design adapter contract and minimal lifecycle hooks (init, run_batch, flush, teardown) — 2d design spike
2) Implement core orchestration that loads adapters by entrypoint and standardizes runner metadata — 3d
3) Build grpc and http adapters by porting existing runner code into plugin modules — 5d
4) Add kv-cache aware adapter that can reuse cached prefixes across runs — 3d
5) Create Docker images and pin runtime deps (torch, transformers, libtorch kernels) for CI matrix — 2d
6) Add CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) matrix and artifact upload to S3/CI artifacts — 3d
7) Migrate two representative scenarios and run smoke/perf comparison, collect traces and dashboards — 4d
8) Postmortem and Ops runbook for onboarding new adapters — 1d
risks: Surface area increase: new plugin API may miss edge cases for older scenarios
Dependency pinning vs OS kernels: pinned libs might diverge from production runtime
KV-cache semantics are subtle; incorrect invalidation could skew results
CI runtime may increase; mitigated by sampling matrix and caching Docker layers
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with Perf infra, Runtime and QA. Agreed on adapter lifecycle hooks and prioritized grpc + http adapters. Action: produce contract doc (Sofia).
2026-02-25: Spike complete. Prototype core loads adapters via setuptools entrypoints. Found threading issues when running http-async adapter in same process — added process-isolation option.
2026-03-02: PR #3342 opened to add adapter loader and core orchestration. Requesting review from @liam.oconnor and @priya.reddy. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadbench/pull/3342

2026-03-08: Implemented grpc adapter and initial kv-cache shim. Local comparisons vs baseline scenario show 2-4% variance in median latency (within noise). Docs draft at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Adapter+Design
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids touching the eval runner used by customer-facing nightly evals; migration will be staged and coordinated with ENG-20345
We will run early adapters behind feature flags and enable process isolation for flaky scenarios
Follow semver for adapter interface; major bumps require coordinated rollout
